# agent-coach

> agent-coach is an open-source, local-first Python CLI that grades and coaches how you prompt Claude Code and OpenAI Codex, using your own conversation history (~/.claude/projects and ~/.codex/sessions) and a rubric built from Anthropic's and OpenAI's official guides and academies.

What it does:
- Scores 11 prompting habits (specific context, done criteria and verification, constraints, handing over real material, scope, plan first, stop points, asking for evidence, course correction, moving repeated rules into CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, one outcome per conversation) on a 0-100 scale.
- Rewrites prompts the user actually typed into better versions, citing the guide section behind each habit.
- Finds "missed responses": turns where the user didn't get what they wanted, classified as prompt gap, agent error, changed mind or external limit. Short prompts are not penalized when context carried the intent.
- Groups recurring prompt gaps into one-line rules and says where to put them (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md, memory, skill, hook).
- Saves every run to ~/.agent-coach/history so progress can be tracked over time.
- Grades through the user's signed-in `claude` or `codex` CLI (no API key), or offline with keyword heuristics.
- Masks secrets and contact details before sending anything to the judge. Zero dependencies, Python 3.9+, MIT license. English and Korean.

Install and run:
pipx install agent-coach   (or uv tool install agent-coach, pip install agent-coach)
agent-coach run

As a plugin (the agent runs it and coaches in chat):
Claude Code: /plugin install agent-coach --marketplace 1017toa/agent-coach, then /agent-coach:coach
Codex: codex plugin marketplace add 1017toa/agent-coach && codex plugin add agent-coach@agent-coach
